lesson_topic: Intellectual Property Law — Bundle of Rights Model (Introductory Module)

principles.evidence: No non-decorative graphics, diagrams, charts, or illustrations are present on any of the five slides; all slides are text-only. The absence of any visual representations means the visual and verbal channels cannot achieve reciprocity, and no graphical quality can be assessed beyond the legibility of the text itself.

The transcript is a verbatim match of the on-screen text across all five slides, with no elaboration, recontextualization, or departure from the written content. On-screen text consists of full prose paragraphs (three per slide) rather than keywords or short labels, exceeding the five-second scan threshold significantly.

All conceptual load is carried by dense on-screen prose paragraphs rather than narration-over-graphics; the visual channel contains no diagrams and is used exclusively for extended written text. The narration is the on-screen text read aloud verbatim, providing zero additional auditory information beyond what is already visible.

No decorative clipart, stock imagery, or tangential anecdotal content is present; all written content is topically relevant to the bundle-of-rights concept. Backgrounds appear clean and uncluttered, and typography and styling appear consistent across the five slides.

A minimal visual hierarchy is present via slide titles and numbered footers, but no arrows, highlights, color contrast, callouts, or bold emphasis mark key elements within the body text. The narration contains no verbal signaling phrases directing learner attention, and no single takeaway per slide is visually or verbally foregrounded.

No graphics, labels, captions, or figures are present, making spatial contiguity between text and visuals impossible to observe or evaluate. Text and title are vertically co-located without a split-attention layout, which is the sole positive observable property under this principle.
